grammar.explanation: This pattern expresses uncertainty or conjecture; in an internal question it means that the speaker wonders about something.
This pattern means to try doing an action and see what happens.
This pattern gives a reason or explanation, meaning because or since. It can also follow an explanatory clause.
This pattern introduces a name, statement, or idea as the topic of a definition or explanation.
This pattern means after doing an action and establishes the starting point for what follows.
This pattern links an action or situation to its regular or immediately following result, meaning when or whenever.
This pattern presents information as an explanation of a situation. It often conveys the reason or background behind an event.
This pattern connects a reason to its consequence, meaning because or since.
This pattern attaches to a verb stem to express wanting to do something. Its negative form expresses not wanting to do it.
This pattern uses a volitional verb form to express an attempt. In the negative, it can express refusal or unwillingness.
This pattern places a verb stem before a movement verb to express the purpose of going or coming.
This pattern marks completion and often adds regret, an unwanted result, or a sense that the event cannot be undone.
This pattern makes the subject the recipient of an action. It also allows statements to be reported without naming who says them.

patternSegments.text: 〜ことができる／〜ことはできる

grammar.explanation: This pattern expresses the ability or possibility of doing an action. Its negative form means cannot.
This pattern presents a condition, meaning if or when an action or change occurs.
This pattern states that someone has never had the experience of doing an action.
This pattern means only or nothing but, emphasizing that all the items belong to the same category.
This pattern gives a direct command. Its form depends on the verb group and sounds forceful.
This pattern describes a change in ability, habit, or state: something becomes possible or begins happening.
This pattern describes an apparent condition based on appearance. Used adverbially, it shows how someone behaves or speaks.
This pattern means that doing an action becomes more frequent.
This pattern means even if or even though, showing that the following result holds despite the stated action.
This pattern limits what happens to just the stated action, meaning only or merely.
This pattern expresses obligation or necessity, meaning must or have to do something.
This pattern politely asks someone not to perform an action.
This pattern adds a prohibition to a dictionary-form verb, giving a forceful command not to do something.
This pattern expresses an intention or plan. With a negative verb, it means intending not to do something.
This pattern links two actions performed at the same time by the same person, meaning while doing.
This pattern connects a negative action to another action, meaning without doing the first action.
